messages:
maya: quick sync — fp8->int8 crossfade operational notes. experimental canary is running, want to capture edgecases and an ops checklist. main goal: reduce token cost while keeping quality delta < 0.5% on our q95 eval set. :eyes:

leo: timeline? how aggressive is the crossfade?

sasha: can we have a short runbook for this? autoscale margins, canary gating, and which telemetry to watch.

maya: plan is 10% canary traffic for 48h, with automatic rollback on either: (a) +1% perplexity on q95, or (b) >3% latency p95 increase. also enable per-layer soft-fallback for heads with KL spike.

jon: FYI I already saw a longctx regression when forcing INT8 on mid layers — +0.6% perplexity on a 16k prompt set. Holding KV cache in FP32 mitigates some of it.

maya: noted. current runtime config keeps KV cache fp32 by default. we only quantize weights/biases.

infra-bot: Deploy event: quant-crossfade/v2 -> prod-canary (3xA100) initiated by @maya at 1718976570. Canary traffic=10%.

ops: checklist suggestion:
- create canary alert (perplexity q95, latency p95)
- add sampling of failure prompts to S3 (prefix: s3://redwood-canary/quant-crossfade/v2/errors)
- enable debug-logs for layer-scale stats for first 2k requests

leo: +1 to storing failed prompts. also capture per-layer activation histograms and sign-preserve rate. those seem predictive of subtle degens.

sasha: example config I propose (short):
```json
{"canary_pct": 0.10, "rollback_criteria": {"perplexity_q95_delta": 0.01, "latency_p95_pct": 0.03}, "per_layer_fallback": {"enabled": true, "kl_threshold": 0.12, "sample_window": 1000}}
```

maya: nice. two operational caveats we discovered: (1) sudden temperature shifts in prompt distribution (e.g., longer prompts with many rare tokens) cause transient KL spikes — our per-layer KL sampling needs smoothing (ema window ~500). (2) quantized matmuls show tiny nondeterminism across GPUs causing different sampling paths if random seeds not pinned at runtime. Pin seeds for the canary.

jon: actionable: add ema window param, and pin rng in runtime for canary. I can PR the runtime patch.

leo: how about fallback granularity? layer-level vs head-level. head-level seems safer but adds perf overhead for checks. tradeoff thoughts?

maya: ops preference = layer-level fallback for initial rollout. Simpler to implement in the kernel and cheaper to check. If we see head-localized failures we can evolve to head-granular fallback. Add telemetry tags for head vs layer events.

sasha: tiny probe command for CI canary runs (local):
```bash
./probe_quant_crossfade --model rwd-7b --quant target=int8 --keep-kv=f32 --warmup 20 --sample 1000 --emit-layer-hist=./out/layer_hist.json
```

maya: capturing this thread's action items: @jon PR runtime seed pin + ema smoothing (eta 1718976700). @sasha add config example to runbook. @leo add S3 sampling hook and alert. ops will create the canary alert now. we’ll reconvene after 48h or on rollback. :thumbsup:

ops: canary alert created: /alerts/quant-crossfade-v2 (thresholds match config). watching. :eyes:

jon: started PR branch: feature/rng-pin-ema, adding tests for reproducibility and a micro-benchmark for longctx. will tag when ready.

maya: thanks all — please post any odd failure samples to this thread so we can triage quickly.

leo: noted. will drop any strange prompts in s3 and ping here. :+1:
